description: The corpus for the x86 compiler-output translator's milestone 0: every program, what it exercises and its intended outcome. scripts/capture-gcc-fixtures.mjs compiles each program with Compiler Explorer at each level into cases/<program>-O<level>.json.gz, and builds the x87 matrix into x87/<form>.json.gz. Every program is compiled as `sourcePaths[language]` with the flag groups below at each of `optimizations`, unless the program narrows its own `optimizations`, replaces a flag (`flags.replace`) or adds some (`flags.add`). Headers are sent at the request's root; `files` are NASM Files beside the source in the Project. An `exit` value is the full value Blink reports; the native status is its low byte. An `exit` outcome's `output`, when present, is what the program writes to standard output, in Blink and natively; without one it writes nothing. `outcomes` overrides `outcome` for one level. A program meant to fail translation may name a `referenceOutcome`, the outcome its GNU as reference must still reach, built at capture time to show the program itself works as written; `note` explains an outcome. `x87Matrix` lists the hand-written x87 forms.

programs.name: cppvague

programs.name: cfprotection
programs.exercises: `-fcf-protection=full` instead of the profile's `none`: `endbr64`, `notrack` jump tables and `.note.gnu.property`; outside the profile
programs.note: Intended to fail translation since 2026-10-04: NASM 3.00 cannot express GCC's `notrack` prefix on the jump-table jump faithfully, so the translator rejects the `notrack jmp` as `unsupported-instruction`, and the profile requires `-fcf-protection=none`. Its GNU as reference, built when the intended outcome was exit 119, is still built and must still exit 119, as evidence that the program itself runs as written.

programs.name: quicksort
programs.exercises: Runtime-library-style generic quicksort through a comparator, on ints and 16-byte records

programs.name: strtol
programs.exercises: Runtime-library-style `strtol`: whitespace, signs, base prefixes, bases 2 to 36, overflow

programs.name: formatter
programs.exercises: Runtime-library-style variadic formatter: `%d %i %u %x %X %c %s %%`, `l`, width, `-` and `0` flags, truncation

programs.name: ctororder
programs.exercises: Unprioritized constructors whose order shows in the result: three `__attribute__((constructor))` functions, whose order the language leaves to GCC, and two global objects, which C++ builds in declaration order, each noting when it ran; `.init_array` holds four entries

programs.name: memberpointers
programs.exercises: Pointers to member functions through a table: ten member functions, one virtual. The Itanium C++ ABI tells a virtual one by the address's low bit, so GCC aligns member functions to 2 bytes (plan note 8)

programs.name: alignedfn
programs.exercises: A function aligned to 64 bytes (`__attribute__((aligned(64)))`), whose address the program checks through a table

programs.name: simwrite
programs.exercises: System calls through inline assembly, as the Environment library's `<sim.h>` makes them: `static inline` wrappers whose register-bound operands GCC substitutes around a `syscall`, inlined, as a local function (called directly at -O0 and -Os, through a volatile pointer at every level) and a `noreturn` exit; a negative errno comes back raw

programs.name: cppsimwrite
programs.exercises: `simwrite`'s `<sim.h>` from C++, under `extern "C"`: `sim_write` from an inline member function (in that function's COMDAT group at -O0) and the `noreturn` `sim_exit_group`

outcome.output:
Hello from C++
Hello from C++

programs.name: cppinlineasm
programs.exercises: A user's `asm("nop")`, and a two-line `asm volatile` with a `memory` clobber in a loop, which GCC unrolls into one `#APP` block holding two statements

programs.name: toplevelasm
programs.exercises: A file-scope `__asm__` defining a global function: an `#APP` block outside any function, with no line markers, a section directive and a label at column 0

programs.name: inlineasmatt
programs.exercises: Inline assembly written in AT&T syntax, which GCC passes through under -masm=intel, substituting its own operand in Intel syntax

programs.name: inlineasmrept
programs.exercises: Inline assembly with a directive outside the rules, `.rept` and its `.endr`
programs.note: The template is GNU as that GCC compiles and GNU as runs, which the reference shows; `.rept` is outside the directives the translator reads, so the block is rejected at its `.rept` and `.endr` lines.

x87Matrix.description: Each form in GCC's -masm=intel spelling, applied to the values in `stack` (top first) loaded from .rodata with fld: 10.0 and 4.0 for st(1) forms, 10.0, 7.0 and 4.0 for st(2) forms, so the operands are always 10 and 4. main stores the stack to memory with fstp, then returns cvtsd2si(destination × 4) + 64, read from the destination register's slot after any pop; every operand order gives a different value below 256, and a form that wrote another register returns 104, 92 or 80 instead. `semantics` and `intelOpcode` are the Intel SDM's; `intended` follows from them.
